events.what: Davies, Gill & Horsley improve upper bounds on Zarankiewicz numbers z(m,n;s,t) via a strengthened linear program
OpenEvolve LLM-guided search finds binary-matrix constructions giving 41 new lower bounds and matching known upper bounds for three exact values, e.g. Z(11,21;3,3)=116
events.ai_basis: The results are obtained using OpenEvolve, an open-source evolutionary algorithm based on Large Language Models (LLMs) that iteratively improves algorithms for generating mathematical constructions

events.what: Saurabh, Afrasyab, Hou, Sadhu preprints report further exact values / bounds on z(m,n;3,3) and z(43;2) by classical methods; Liu & Song treats a limited augmented variant

judgement.doubts: The bullet asks for the extremal function in general; finitely many exact values for specific (m,n,s,t) are treated like new table entries (F3, degree–diameter) — bound-level movement, not a case settlement. Arguably they are just instances. Either way the status is progress or lower, not partial. Davies–Gill–Horsley and Bhan et al. move different entries at the same tier, so by step 4 the stronger AI role (generated) applies. The model names in the Bhan et al. record are uncertain because of fetch artifacts, but that does not change the code.

corrections.why: F14: the status is progress (new bounds and finitely many exact entries of a still-open extremal function), and a progress row carries a null direction.

other: kept as progress. The three exact values are specific table entries of the function the bullet asks for, and they bound it; they are not a restriction that settles a case. Reading them as a case would make this partial, so the call is doubtful.
